subsystems.name: Reentry heat shield
subsystems.role: protects the stage as it comes back through the atmosphere at orbital speed.
parts: mechanical attachments that allow thermal expansion

subsystems.name: Engine section
subsystems.role: performs the insertion burn and later the landing burn with the same engines.

subsystems.name: Propellant tanks and structure
subsystems.role: holds the propellant and carries launch and reentry loads.

subsystems.name: Attitude control and aerosurfaces
subsystems.role: keeps the stage pointed correctly while it is in the plasma and during the final descent.

subsystems.name: Guidance, navigation and control
subsystems.role: flies the reentry and lands the stage on a target within metres.

subsystems.name: Recovery and refurbishment infrastructure
subsystems.role: gets the stage back on a pad and ready to fly again.
parts: catch tower, landing pad or parachute recovery

buildSteps.title: Choose the recovery architecture
buildSteps.detail: Decide whether the whole stage comes back, only the engine section returns, and whether it lands on legs, is caught by a tower, or comes down under parachutes. Thermal protection is dead weight, so every kilogram of shield is a kilogram of lost payload.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate tanks and structure
buildSteps.detail: Thin-gauge stainless steel or aluminium-lithium sheet is rolled, friction-stir welded into tanks, and stiffened so the stage survives both launch loads and the bending loads of reentry.

buildSteps.title: Fix the thermal protection
buildSteps.detail: Thousands of tiles or metallic panels are bonded or bolted to the windward side, with gaps sized so the hot structure can expand without cracking the shield.

buildSteps.title: Integrate engines and control surfaces
buildSteps.detail: Deep-throttling restartable engines are fitted along with flaps or grid fins and small thrusters that hold the stage at the right angle during reentry.

buildSteps.title: Launch and separate
buildSteps.detail: The stage fires to place its payload in orbit, then reserves enough propellant for a deorbit burn and a landing burn — a reserve that directly cuts payload mass.

buildSteps.title: Deorbit and reenter
buildSteps.detail: A short retro burn drops the perigee into the atmosphere, and the stage flies through the plasma sheath, shedding roughly 7.8 km/s of orbital velocity while the shield surface reaches around 1,500 °C.

buildSteps.title: Fly the terminal descent
buildSteps.detail: Thrusters settle the propellant to the bottom of the tanks, guidance steers to the recovery point, and the engines relight at low throttle for a controlled touchdown or a mid-air catch.

buildSteps.title: Recover, inspect and refly
buildSteps.detail: Engineers inspect tiles, engines and structure, replace what is damaged, and return the stage to the pad — the cost of this turnaround decides whether recovery pays.

prerequisites.why: ablative shields survive one reentry only; a reusable shield must take many cycles with minimal repair, which has proven difficult since the Shuttle era.
boosters have landed and refly routinely since 2015, but they reenter at far lower speed than an orbital stage.
a landing burn needs multiple ignitions and precise low thrust.
propellant must be settled and kept liquid during a long coast before the deorbit and landing burns.
if a stage needs months of work between flights, the savings in hardware vanish.

pathway.milestone: orbit-capable upper stages regularly reenter and make controlled soft splashdowns, while first-stage boosters land and refly
pathway.unlocks: real flight data on reentry loads, tile performance and terminal guidance.

pathway.milestone: subscale demonstrators prove vertical takeoff and landing of a second-stage-shaped vehicle
pathway.unlocks: confidence that a full-size upper stage can be flown to a pinpoint landing.

pathway.milestone: first intact recovery and reflight of an orbital-class upper stage
pathway.unlocks: a genuine path to a fully reusable launch stack, cutting the hardware cost per flight.

pathway.milestone: routine reuse with short turnaround and orbital refuelling
pathway.unlocks: launch cost dominated by propellant and operations, supporting large-scale space infrastructure.
